The simulator can expose five events: protection-inventory, service-modification-attempted, policy-write-attempted, persistence-attempted, and telemetry-interruption. Each event writes structured data to a temporary exercise directory and a separate remote collector. The event payload includes a case ID, fake product name, fake service, fake path, timestamp, and operator. It must not call service-management APIs, edit the registry, alter endpoint policy, inject into another process, delete files, create startup entries, or suppress logs.

A simple event function is:

def emit(stage, fake_target, case_id):
    event = {"stage": stage, "target": fake_target, "case": case_id}
    local_log.write(event)
    remote_log.send(event)

Before the run, record processes, services, policies, startup items, hashes, identity state, DNS, and network connections. Emit one stage at a time and verify that tamper protection, policy authorization, startup monitoring, and endpoint-health alerts respond as expected. Correlate parent-child process events, file writes, authentication records, DNS, and egress telemetry. Keep the remote collector independent so the simulator cannot erase the only evidence.

The report should include the expected alert, observed alert, time to detection, analyst action, recovery step, and gap. Restore the snapshot after each scenario and compare the post-run inventory with the baseline. Recommended controls include least privilege, signed configuration, protected service interfaces, application allowlisting, startup monitoring, immutable remote logs, credential rotation, backup recovery, and network isolation.

A red team can obtain an approved commercial test agent if it needs real control-plane behavior. Written scope, a named owner, and a rollback plan are required. This produces measurable prevention, detection, investigation, and recovery results without creating a virus or a reusable mechanism for disabling endpoint protection.

Assign a named owner and approval record to every scenario so failures can be audited.
